classification.difficultyReason: Infer two isosceles triangles from equal square and equilateral sides, then link their base angles to the square corners and the target triangle.

content.prompt: Square $ABCD$ shares a side with equilateral triangle $AXD$. Find the measure of $\angle BXC$.

spec.description: Upright square ABCD containing equilateral triangle AXD, with apex X upward and additional segments BX and CX. Source cyan fill is omitted because it supplies no mathematical given.
spec.mathematics: ABCD is a square; AX=XD=AD. A is bottom left, B top left, C top right and D bottom right. All four segments AX, DX, BX and CX are retained.
spec.answerVisibility: The question figure contains only the original labels and segments; no angle values or answer annotations are shown.

inlines.text: Use the equal base angles in triangles ABX and DCX, then the angle sum of triangle BXC.

answer.worked:
Since $ABCD$ is a square and $AXD$ is equilateral, $AB=AX$ and $DC=DX$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAX&=90^{\circ}-60^{\circ}\\\angle BAX&=30^{\circ}\\\angle ABX&=\frac{180^{\circ}-30^{\circ}}{2}\\\angle ABX&=75^{\circ}\\\angle XBC&=90^{\circ}-75^{\circ}\\\angle XBC&=15^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Similarly, $\angle BCX=15^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle BXC&=180^{\circ}-15^{\circ}-15^{\circ}\\\angle BXC&=150^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
